title: Plant Structures and Their Functions
seo_title: Grade 4 Plant Structures Worksheets: Roots, Stems, Leaves, Flowers and Adaptations
standard_text: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on plant structures (NGSS 4-LS1-1): roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, thorns and bark, labeled plant diagrams and structures that help plants survive. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Every plant structure has a job.
key_sub: Roots take in water, stems hold the plant up, leaves make food, and flowers make seeds.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants have structures (parts) that help them grow, survive and make new plants. Each structure has a job:

  • Roots: take in water and minerals and hold the plant in place.
  • Stem: holds the plant up; tubes inside carry water and food.
  • Leaves: use sunlight to make food.
  • Flowers: make seeds. Fruits protect and spread seeds.
  • Thorns, spines and bark: protect the plant.

Plants in different places have structures that fit their surroundings, like the thick, waxy stem of a cactus.

Example

Which part of a plant makes food?

Food is made with sunlight.

Leaves catch sunlight.

Answer: the leaves

Example

How do a cactus's spines help it?

Spines are sharp.

Animals do not want to bite them.

Answer: They protect it from animals that would eat it.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil. Roots take in water and minerals; leaves make food.
  • Thinking flowers are only for decoration. They make seeds.
  • Forgetting internal structures, like the tubes inside a stem.

faq.q: What are the main parts of a plant?
faq.a: Roots, stem, leaves and flowers. Many plants also have fruits and seeds.

faq.q: Do plants get food from the soil?
faq.a: No. Roots take in water and minerals. Leaves use sunlight, air and water to make the plant's food.

faq.q: How do structures help plants survive?
faq.a: Thorns and spines protect plants, waxy coatings save water, and fruits help spread seeds to new places.
